sentences.text: Shri Vasant Roland Daniel, learned counsel with Shri Ne  Soni, counsel for the petitioner.
Shri Kamal Kumar Tiwari appearing on behalf of Advocate  ORDER Heard and perused the case diary.

This is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in relation to FIR/Crime No.134/2024 dated (not mentioned), registered at Police Station-M.G. Road, District Indore, for the offence under Section 420, 467, 468, 471, 474 and 120-B/34 of IPC.
The applicant is in jail since 15.05.2024.

Earlier application of the applicant was dismissed as simple withdrawn on 26.04.2024 passed in MCRC No.16713/2024.
2.

As per prosecution story, brief facts of the case as per the application so submitted are as under:-

That, the complainant, Upper Commissioner Waterworks and Drainage Municipal Corporation, Indore sent a written complaint dt. 02.04.2024 to police station M.G Road Indore regarding lodging an FIR for preparing forged documents for the work of laying sewer lines in the drainage department and showing a completion certificate Moh. sentences.text:
That, the non-applicant no. 1 registered the case against Moh. Sajid, Moh. Siddique, Renu Vadera, Moh. Zakir and Rahul Vadera U/s 420, 467, 468, 471, 474, 120-B and 34 of IPC in crime no.
134/24.

That, the allegation in short as per the FIR is that all the accused prepared the forged file of construction of sewer lines through the forged signature and twenty bills have been presented in the account department by the said five contractors and the proprietors of the firms by preparing fake and forged documents in a fraudulent manner as per the above facts, the note sheet prepare after the examination and the file of the bunch of the twenty bills sent by the accounts branch and the form of signature of the officers in it, the comparative form of work order, the comparative form of bills incoming no. the comparative form of the outgoing number sent to the account branch and the copies of the complete file dt.03.03.2024, Sunday the complainant was working in the office from 11.45 am to 7.45 pm for further action on the pending cases, from where the trunk of the vehicle was opened and stolen the original documents related to the offence by the unknown persons and these files were burned and destroyed by the accused Moh.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3271 3 MCRC-53955-2024 Zakir, Rajendra Sharma,
Moh Imraan, Mousam Vyas, Ehteshaam and Aashu.
On the complaint of Sunil Gupta, the police station registered a crime no. 68/24 U/s 379 of the IPC and started the investigation at that time.
The present matter has been registered on the basis of photocopy.

That, the allegation against Moh.
Sajid, Moh. Siddique and Renu Vadera in the furtherance of common intention prepared 21 fake work order files of drainage depart.

By forging bills of fake work and presented them in the concerned department of the Municipal Corporation and through separate bills of RS.1,50,87,680/-
received in the bank account of M/s Green Constructions Rs. 42,000,00/- lakhs in the bank account of Green Construction belongs to the applicant and the money was distributed among all the officers and employees.
3. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant has been implicated in the present case falsely.
It is further submitted that the applicant is 77 years old person, suffering from various ailments.

It is further submitted that in the present case, the complainant himself has admitted that the original files/bills were stolen from his car and he himself has admitted that it is his mistake which ought not to be done by him.
As per the prosecution case itself, one FIR was lodged against unknown persons for said theft on the Direction of Superior authorities.

The documents so produced for the bills, the complainant himself has admitted that all the bills were well verified by himself, therefore, it cannot be said that the applicants, who was a contractor has committed the offence.

As per the provisions of Section 65 (c) of the Evidence Act, photocopies of original documents not be treated as NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3271 4 MCRC-53955-2024 secondary evidence if original stands theft.

Learned Senior counsel has further submitted that the complainant himself has received the original bills which are alleged to be prepared by forging by the applicant and other co- accused whereas the photocopies of the same has been provided by the complainant to the investigation authorities.

It is also submitted that in the present case, the investigation agency has sent the photocopies to the FSL for verification of the Moh. Siddique vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172495645/
2 signatures of the person who committed forgery, it is not possible to ascertain about the signatures on the photocopies of signatory person at any cost.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is the complainant who has lost the original documents and he has also admitted his negligence.

4. Leaned counsel for the applicant further submits that no Investigating Agency, Police or Magistrate can take cognizance on the basis of providing photocopies in criminal jurisprudence whereas the originals were lost as per the provisions of Section 65 of the Indian Evidence Act.
Therefore, the applicant has not played any role in the offence.

Learned Senior counsel for the applicant further submitted that co-accused persons namely Murlidhar, Anil Garg, Samar Singh Parmar, Uday Singh Bhadoriya, Mohd. Imran have already granted regular bail by this Court whereas one of the co-accused Renu Vadhera has already been enlarged on bail by trial Court even after similar allegations and one of the co-accused Mohd. Aihatesham Khan and Bilkis Khan were granted anticipatory bail by this Court on 16.10.2024 because Aihatesham Khan has deposited entire amount in another crime number 171/2024 in compliance of the directions of Hon'ble Apex Court.

Similarly, in same Crime Number i.e. in 171/2024 of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:3271 5 MCRC-53955-2024 M.G. Road, accused Jahid Khan has also granted regular bail subject to depoist 50% of the embezzled amount in that crime on completion of approximately eight months of custody period.

entities.text:
NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:3271 5 MCRC-53955-2024 M.G. Road
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: However, learned counsel for the applicant, at the end of arguments has also submitted that the applicant is also ready to deposit 50% of the amount received by the applicant in his account.
Therefore the applicant is also entitled to get bail.

5. On the contrary, learned Government Advocate for the State has opposed the prayer by submitting that the persons who have been granted bail by this Court were only the employees of the Indore Nagar Nigam whereas the applicant is one of the main accused.
It is also submitted that in the present case, the applicant has received approximately Rs.42,00,000/- in his account.
6. I have heard the counsel for the parties and perused the record.

7. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, the fact that the applicant is aged about 77 years old and he is ready to depoist 50% of the entire amount as alleged by the prosecution in the present crime and custody period of approximately eight months, without commenting upon the merits of the case, this Court deems it appropriate to allow this application.
Accordingly, the application is allowed.

8. It is directed that subject to depoist 50% of the total amount of Rs.42,00,000/- i.e.
Rs.21,00,000/- before the trial Court, applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond also in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3271 6 MCRC-53955-2024 the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3 of BNSS,2023.
9.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
